# OSSL to ring trial transfer


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

> Pretraining, the zero-shot experiment, the instrument model, the sensitivity check, the augmentation and fine-tuning on two instruments have run. The other experiments below are still to come.

This project tests whether CNN models of soil mid-infrared (MIR) spectra, trained on the [Open Soil Spectral Library (OSSL)](https://explorer.soilspectroscopy.org/), transfer to other spectrometers. It uses the ring trial of [Safanelli et al. (2023)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.geoderma.2023.116724), in which 20 laboratories scanned the same 70 soils, each with its own instrument and procedure. A Shimadzu instrument in Japan (`Hokudai`) also scanned 59 of the soils. The targets are organic carbon, clay, pH and exchangeable potassium (Kex).

The ring trial keeps the soils fixed and changes only the instrument. 60 of the soils come from KSSL, the largest part of OSSL. One of the instruments, the IAEA Thermo Nicolet, also measured the Fukushima soils of [`ossl-fuku-transfer`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/ossl-fuku-transfer/). There the OSSL Kex model failed on the Fukushima spectra, and it is not settled whether the instrument or the soils caused it. If the model works on the IAEA spectra of these soils, the instrument is not the main cause.

The audience is soil scientists who transfer spectral models between instruments, and the readers of `ossl-fuku-transfer`.

## Design

- Question: the ring trial keeps the soils fixed and changes only the instrument, so it isolates cross-calibration. The project tests whether a CNN pretrained on OSSL can give the same prediction for a soil on every instrument. Exchangeable K is the main property, because of its role in the remediation of soils after a nuclear accident, and because it has no direct absorption band. Clay is the control, with a direct signal and a known cause for its bias on KSSL.
- Data: soilspecdata’s `load_ringtrial` returns one `Spectra` per instrument, with the wet chemistry of the 70 soils.
- Pretraining: OSSL v1.2 without 38 KSSL samples that are ring-trial soils. Their OSSL spectra correlate with the KSSL instrument’s ring-trial spectra at 0.99999 or more, and their clay, pH and Kex values are identical. The remaining 22 KSSL soils and the 10 NAPT soils have no match in OSSL.
- Model: soilspecdl’s default `SpectralCNN`, the same CNN as in `ossl-fuku-transfer`, so the results of the two projects compare directly.
- Split: on each instrument, grouped k-fold cross-validation over all 70 soils, repeated with different fold assignments. Near-duplicate soils, such as RT_04, RT_05, RT_07, RT_13 and RT_15, stay in one fold. The paper’s Kennard-Stone split (50 calibration and 20 test soils) is not used: it is optimistic, and its test set has only 20 soils.
- Scores: Lin’s CCC, the paper’s main metric, and R². Every method uses the same folds, so methods are compared soil by soil, with paired tests.
- Experiments:
  1.  Zero-shot (`02_zero_shot`): the OSSL models on every instrument, with no adaptation. The comparison with the paper’s Cubist, MBL and PLSR transfer results is not done yet.
  2.  Instrument model (`03_instrument_model`): the difference between each instrument and KSSL, modelled with a few physical effects that all its soils share.
  3.  Sensitivity (`04_sensitivity`): how much the predictions change under each of these effects.
  4.  Augmentation (`05_augment`, `06_aug_pretrain`): pretraining with random instrument effects applied to the OSSL spectra, then zero-shot scoring on every instrument.
  5.  Fine-tuning (`07_finetune`): fine-tuning on the soils of one instrument, and ridge regression on frozen block-4 features, from three pretrained models, against PLSR trained only on those soils. The PLSR preprocessing is that of mirzai: SNV, a first-derivative Savitzky-Golay filter and removal of the CO₂ band. It has run for K and clay on KSSL and IAEA. `08_recalibrate` compares it with linear recalibration, AdaBN and a refit of the head. The other instruments, growing numbers of training soils, and the comparison of the gains with the paper’s instrument clusters and spectral dissimilarity are not done yet.
- Aim: to understand what changes in the CNN under augmentation and fine-tuning, not to rank the methods by one score.

## Notebooks

- [`00_data`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/ossl-rt-transfer/data.html): loads the spectra and the instrument table, groups the near-duplicate soils, and lists the 38 ring-trial soils that are in OSSL.
- [`01_pretrain`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/ossl-rt-transfer/pretrain.html): trains one CNN each for clay, pH and K on OSSL, without those 38 soils, on SNV spectra, with the training settings of `ossl-fuku-transfer` but 80 epochs instead of 20.
- [`02_zero_shot`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/ossl-rt-transfer/zero_shot.html): scores the three models on all 21 ring-trial instruments, with no adaptation.
- [`03_instrument_model`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/ossl-rt-transfer/instrument_model.html): models the difference between each instrument and KSSL with a few physical effects shared by all soils, such as a gain, a baseline and a wavenumber shift.
- [`04_sensitivity`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/ossl-rt-transfer/sensitivity.html): measures how much the predictions of the three models change when one physical instrument effect, such as a wavenumber shift or a broadening, is applied to OSSL spectra.
- [`05_augment`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/ossl-rt-transfer/augment.html): applies random shift, stretch, broadening, contrast, gain and baseline to OSSL spectra during pretraining, one transform for each effect, and compares the clay and K models with and without them.
- [`06_aug_pretrain`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/ossl-rt-transfer/aug_pretrain.html): finds how many epochs the augmented clay and K models need, and scores the augmented models that fine-tuning will start from.
- [`07_finetune`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/ossl-rt-transfer/finetune.html): fine-tunes the clay and K models on the KSSL and IAEA soils from three starting models, and compares fine-tuning, ridge regression on frozen features, zero-shot and PLSR, against wet chemistry and against the KSSL prediction.
- [`08_recalibrate`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/ossl-rt-transfer/recalibrate.html): compares fine-tuning with cheaper corrections fitted on the same soils: a bias, or a slope and bias, on the zero-shot predictions, AdaBN, and a refit of the head.

## Set-up

The project uses the soilspec packages ([soilspecdl](https://github.com/franckalbinet/soilspecdl), [soilspecdata](https://github.com/franckalbinet/soilspecdata) and [soilspectfm](https://github.com/franckalbinet/soilspectfm)) as editable installs from sibling folders:

    soilspec/
      ossl-rt-transfer/
      soilspecdl/
      soilspecdata/
      soilspectfm/

Clone the four repositories into one folder, then, in `ossl-rt-transfer/`:

``` sh
uv sync --extra dev
```

The ring-trial data are not public. This repository does not contain them. With access to them, put them in `data/ringtrial/` in the workspace folder, beside the project folders. `nbdev-test` skips the cells that read them. Run `nbdev-test --flags rtdata` to include them.
